summary: A man who cannot hear or speak can marry and divorce with signs. A wife who becomes a deaf-mute can still be divorced, but a husband who becomes one, or loses his mind, can never divorce, because a man divorces only by his own will.

chunks.en: A deaf-mute man who married a woman who can hear and speak,
chunks.st: With regard to a deaf-mute who married a halakhically competent woman,

words.note: Someone who cannot hear or speak.

chunks.en: and a man who can hear who married a deaf-mute woman:
chunks.st: and a halakhically competent man who married a deaf-mute:

chunks.en: if he wants, he may send her away,
chunks.st: If either man wants to divorce his wife, he may divorce her,

chunks.en: and if he wants, he may keep her.
chunks.st: and if he wants to maintain her as his wife, he may maintain her.

chunks.en: Just as he marries with signs,
chunks.st: The reason why a deaf-mute man can divorce his wife is that just as he marries her by intimation, i.e., his marriage is not performed by explicit speech, as deaf-mutes rely on gestures,

chunks.en: so he divorces with signs.
chunks.st: so too, he divorces her by intimation.

chunks.en: A man who can hear who married a woman who can hear,
chunks.st: Likewise, in the case of a halakhically competent man who married a halakhically competent woman,

chunks.en: and she became a deaf-mute: if he wants, he may send her away,
chunks.st: and she later became a deaf-mute: If he wants to divorce his wife, he may divorce her, as a wife does not have to have intellectual capacity to receive a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: and if he wants, he may keep her.
chunks.st: and if he wants to maintain her as his wife, he may maintain her.

chunks.en: If she lost her mind, he may not send her away.
chunks.explain: She cannot look after her get, and she needs his care.
chunks.st: If she became an imbecile, he may not divorce her, i.e., a bill of divorce is ineffective in this case.

chunks.en: If he became a deaf-mute or lost his mind,
chunks.st: If he became a deaf-mute or an imbecile after they were married,

chunks.en: he can never send her away.
chunks.st: he may never divorce her, as he does not have the legal competence to give a bill of divorce.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said:

chunks.en: "Why may a woman who became a deaf-mute be divorced,
chunks.st: For what reason is the halakha that in the case of the woman who becomes a deaf-mute, her husband may divorce her,

chunks.en: but a man who became a deaf-mute cannot divorce?"
chunks.st: but in the case of the man who becomes a deaf-mute, he may not divorce his wife?
chunks.stMore: If the bill of divorce written by someone who formerly possessed all his senses and later became a deaf-mute is invalid, it stands to reason that it should not be valid when she becomes a deaf-mute either.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to him:

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ דוֹמֶה הָאִישׁ הַמְגָרֵשׁ לְאִשָּׁה מִתְגָּרֶשֶׁת,
chunks.en: "A man who divorces is not like a woman being divorced,
chunks.st: The man who divorces his wife is not similar to the woman who is divorced,

chunks.en: because a woman is divorced whether she wants or not,
chunks.st: as the woman is divorced whether she is willing or unwilling. Since the woman’s consent is not required, she may be divorced even if she is a deaf-mute.

chunks.en: but a man divorces only when he wants."
chunks.st: And, conversely, the man divorces his wife only willingly, and therefore the bill of divorce of a deaf-mute, who is not legally competent, is ineffective.

summary: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgedah testified that a deaf-mute girl married off by her father can be divorced with a get. The Sages said the same is true of a woman who became a deaf-mute.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgedah testified
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgada testified

chunks.en: about a deaf-mute girl whose father married her off,
chunks.st: with regard to a female deaf-mute whose father married her off when she was a minor, which means her marriage was valid by Torah law,

chunks.en: that she can go out with a get.
chunks.st: that she can be divorced with a bill of divorce even when she matures and is no longer under her father’s authority, despite the fact that she is not legally competent.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to him:

chunks.en: "This one, too, is like her."
chunks.explain: A woman who became a deaf-mute after marrying.
chunks.st: This woman, too, has a similar status.
chunks.stMore: In other words, a woman who possessed all her faculties and later became a deaf-mute is comparable to a minor whose marriage was valid by Torah law and later, when she matured and was no longer under the authority of her father, received a bill of divorce. Both of these women can receive a bill of divorce, in accordance with the principle stated in the previous paragraph.

summary: Two brothers, one deaf-mute and one who can hear, married two sisters who can hear. If the deaf-mute dies, his widow is free. If the brother who can hear dies, the deaf-mute must divorce his wife, and the widow is forbidden to him forever.

chunks.st: what should the halakhically competent brother married to the halakhically competent sister do?

chunks.en: She goes out because she is his wife's sister.
chunks.st: His brother’s wife is released without levirate marriage or ḥalitza, due to the prohibition with regard to a wife’s sister.

chunks.en: If the one who hears, husband of the one who hears, died,

chunks.st: what should the deaf-mute brother married to the halakhically competent sister do?

chunks.en: He sends away his wife with a get,
chunks.st: He divorces his wife with a bill of divorce, as his wife’s sister came before him for levirate marriage by Torah law, and the legal status of her marriage and her levirate marriage is higher than his own marriage, which applies only by rabbinic law.

chunks.en: and his brother's wife is forbidden forever.
chunks.explain: He cannot do chalitzah, since he cannot speak.
chunks.st: And his brother’s wife is forbidden to him forever, and there is no remedy for her.
chunks.stMore: He cannot marry her, as by rabbinic law she is the sister of his ex-wife, nor can he exempt her by means of ḥalitza, as he is a deaf-mute.
